title: Touch and ablution: differences of legal schools
en: This is an editorial summary of the ablution section, not a quotation. The fatwa reports differing positions: Shafi'i jurists treat the described skin contact as invalidating ablution even without desire; Abu Hanifa does not treat touch alone as invalidating it; the Maliki discussion distinguishes contact accompanied by desire. It also records different reports from Ahmad. These are scholarly interpretations, not a single unanimous ruling. This note concerns ablution, not permission for unrelated physical contact.

title: Touching one's wife without a barrier
en: Editorial summary, not a verbatim quotation: this institutional answer describes the Shafi'i position for direct contact with one's wife. Contact of the skin without an intervening barrier invalidates ablution in that position, including accidental contact. Hair, teeth and nails are excluded in the stated answer. The ruling is expressly school-specific and should not be represented as agreement among all schools.
